name: Sodium session-key validation bypass
summary: Sodium's executeWithSodiumAuthSession signature path accepted an attacker-chosen session key with no owner authorization proof, letting forged user operations consume more than 300 wallets' EntryPoint gas deposits.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

limitations: Target identity and code history came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/sodium.json; no semantic revalidation was inherited.
The executing code artifact and its code hash have not been established in structured evidence.
One or more target block, transaction, ordering, or creator anchors remain unresolved.

sources.note: verified Sodium implementation deployed by 0x0f369f61983cb0c4a432e4a81aaaa24f2d48be45 in tx 0x259d0c343896630f0a94cd7d4ff69fd489d424618368aa362a37b9662e21cce4; sampled victim wallets pointed to it before the attack

deployment-basis recheck: same implementation contract as the Lumi row. Its runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 142595379 and the incident block 483046805 and it holds no implementation slot of any kind; callTracer shows the exploit tx DELEGATECALLs *into* it from the wallet proxies (executeWithSodiumAuthSession / validateUserOp 0x3a871cdd), so the executing code is its own 2023 bytecode. The two delegatecall sites inside it are OpenZeppelin Address.functionDelegateCall and the caller-supplied Enum.Operation.DelegateCall path, neither an upgrade point. Deployment is exact; 995.0 days.
